course.title: AP World History: Modern

stimulusBlocks.attribution: Thomas Paine, English-born writer living in Philadelphia, Common Sense, pamphlet published in January 1776
stimulusBlocks.citation: Thomas Paine, Common Sense (1776), introduction and parts 1 and 3. Project Gutenberg eBook #147.
stimulusBlocks.note: “The continent” is the thirteen British colonies in North America; “the island” is Great Britain.
stimulusBlocks.text:
The cause of America is in a great measure the cause of all mankind. . . .

Society in every state is a blessing, but government even in its best state is but a necessary evil; in its worst state an intolerable one . . . .

Small islands not capable of protecting themselves, are the proper objects for kingdoms to take under their care; but there is something very absurd, in supposing a continent to be perpetually governed by an island. . . .

O ye that love mankind! Ye that dare oppose, not only the tyranny, but the tyrant, stand forth! Every spot of the old world is overrun with oppression. Freedom hath been hunted round the globe.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 5.2 key concept: people around the world developed a new sense of commonality, and slave resistance challenged existing authorities in the Americas, as in the Haitian Revolution
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the Haitian Revolution, 1791–1804
stimulusBlocks.text:
Saint-Domingue, a French colony on the island of Hispaniola, was the richest colony in the Caribbean, producing much of Europe's sugar and coffee with the labor of about 500,000 enslaved Africans. In 1791, enslaved people rose in revolt. Under leaders such as Toussaint Louverture, they defeated French, Spanish, and British forces, and in 1804 declared the independent nation of Haiti.

Haiti was the only state founded by a successful revolt of enslaved people. Its independence alarmed slaveholders across the Americas, and France demanded a large payment from Haiti in 1825 in exchange for recognition.

choiceExplanations: France demanded payment for recognition in 1825 but did not rule Haiti again.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 5.2 key concept: discontent with monarchist and imperial rule encouraged the development of political ideologies, and Enlightenment ideas inspired independence movements in Latin America
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing Latin American independence movements, 1810–1825
stimulusBlocks.text:
When Napoleon invaded Spain in 1808, Spanish rule in the Americas was thrown into confusion. Creole elites, people of Spanish descent born in the Americas, had long resented that the highest offices went to men born in Spain. Leaders such as Simón Bolívar and José de San Martín led armies that won independence for most of Spanish South America by 1825.

Independence did not overturn the colonial social order. Creoles took the top positions, while most Indigenous people, mestizos, and people of African descent remained poor and excluded from power.

choices: the rise of Indigenous governments
continuity in Spanish rule over the new nations after independence
continuity in social hierarchy after independence
the end of all inequality in Latin America
questions.explanation: Creoles took power while the poor remained excluded.
choiceExplanations: Creoles took power.
Spanish rule ended.
Creoles took power while the poor remained excluded.
Inequality continued.
questions.distinguisher: Spanish rule ended; the social hierarchy continued.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 5.2 key concept: nationalism, a sense of commonality based on language, religion, social customs, and territory, led to the unification of Italy and Germany
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing Italian and German unification, 1848–1871
stimulusBlocks.text:
In the early 1800s, Italy and Germany were divided into many states. Nationalists argued that people who shared a language and culture should share a government. In Italy, Count Camillo di Cavour, prime minister of Piedmont-Sardinia, used diplomacy and war, while Giuseppe Garibaldi's volunteers conquered southern Italy. The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in 1861.

In Germany, the Prussian minister Otto von Bismarck fought three wars, against Denmark, Austria, and France, and proclaimed the German Empire in 1871. Bismarck said great questions would be decided by “iron and blood,” not by speeches.

questions.distinguisher: Both involved war, so they were not peaceful.

questions.prompt: Which detail best shows the importance of disease in the outcome of the revolution?
choices: Toussaint Louverture was captured and taken to France

questions.explanation: Yellow fever weakened the French expedition and helped the rebels win.
choiceExplanations: Louverture's capture shows French success, not the role of disease.
Defeating armies shows the rebels' strength, not disease.

questions.distinguisher: The rebels fought well, but the passage names yellow fever specifically as what hurt the French.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 5.2 key concept: the Haitian Revolution began as a slave revolt and ended slavery and French rule in Saint-Domingue
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the Haitian Revolution, 1791–1804
stimulusBlocks.text:
In 1791 enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue, the richest sugar colony in the Caribbean, rose in revolt. Toussaint Louverture, a formerly enslaved man, became the leading general. After France abolished slavery in 1794, he fought for the French Republic against Spanish and British invaders, defeated his rivals, and by 1801 governed the whole island. In 1802 Napoleon sent an expedition to restore French control and slavery. Louverture was captured, but the rebels under Jean-Jacques Dessalines defeated the French army, which suffered heavily from yellow fever.

On January 1, 1804, Dessalines declared the independent nation of Haiti, the first nation founded by a successful uprising of enslaved people.
